claim: On 7 October 2023 Hamas led a mass attack on southern Israel.
notes: Approximately 6,000 attackers from Gaza; deadliest single day for Jews since the Holocaust.

claim: Approximately 1,200 people were killed in the 7 October 2023 attack.
notes: Best current official figure is 1,195 killed (815 civilians); '~1,200' is the standard rounded figure.

claim: About 250-251 people were abducted to Gaza on 7 October 2023.
notes: Settled official figure is 251 hostages taken.

claim: A temporary truce ran 24-30 November 2023 (4 days plus extensions).
notes: Qatar-mediated; initial 4-day deal extended twice; ended 1 December 2023.

claim: About 105 hostages were released during the November 2023 pause.
notes: 105 civilians freed: 81 from Israel, 23 Thai nationals, 1 Filipino.

claim: About 240 Palestinian prisoners were released during the November 2023 pause.
notes: 240 total: 107 minors and 133 adults; roughly three-quarters not convicted of any crime.

claim: Israel struck the Iranian consulate compound in Damascus on 1 April 2024, killing IRGC generals.
notes: Trigger cited by Iran for the April 2024 direct attack.

claim: Iran launched a direct drone/missile attack on Israel overnight 13-14 April 2024.
notes: ~170 drones, at least 30 cruise missiles, 120+ ballistic missiles (~320 projectiles); ~99% intercepted with US/UK/France/Jordan assistance.

claim: Iran launched a second direct missile attack on Israel on 1 October 2024.
notes: ~180-200 ballistic missiles (Israeli media 181; IRGC claimed 200); one indirect fatality in the West Bank; retaliation for Nasrallah killing and Lebanon ground operation.

claim: Israel conducted retaliatory strikes on Iranian military targets on 26 October 2024.
notes: Covered by Commons Library briefing 'Israel-Iran October 2024' (CBP-10113).

claim: Hezbollah pagers exploded across Lebanon on 17 September 2024.
notes: Mossad operation; ~12 killed, ~2,750-3,000 wounded on day one.

claim: Hezbollah walkie-talkies exploded on 18 September 2024.
notes: ~30 killed, 750+ wounded; combined two-day toll ~42 killed, ~3,500 wounded.

claim: Hassan Nasrallah was killed by Israeli strikes on 27 September 2024.
notes: Massive bunker-buster strike on Hezbollah HQ in Beirut's southern suburbs.

claim: Israel began a ground operation in southern Lebanon in October 2024.
notes: Ground incursion launched 1 October 2024.

claim: An Israel-Hezbollah ceasefire was announced 26 November and took effect 27 November 2024.
notes: 60-day framework built on UNSCR 1701 principles; later marred by continuing Israeli strikes and incomplete withdrawal.

claim: Yahya Sinwar was killed on 16 October 2024 in Rafah; confirmed 17 October.
notes: Chance encounter with IDF patrol in Tal as-Sultan; ID confirmed via dental and fingerprint records.

claim: Ismail Haniyeh was assassinated in Tehran on 31 July 2024.
notes: Killed in IRGC guesthouse after Pezeshkian's inauguration; Israel confirmed responsibility in December 2024.

claim: The Assad regime collapsed on 8 December 2024.
notes: HTS/SNA/Southern Operations Room offensive; Assad granted asylum in Moscow.

claim: Israel destroyed most of Syria's strategic military assets after Assad's fall and entered the Golan buffer zone.
notes: 70-80% of strategic capabilities destroyed within ~48 hours; ~400 km2 buffer zone seized including the Syrian summit of Mount Hermon; Netanyahu declared the 1974 disengagement agreement collapsed.

claim: Ahmed al-Sharaa became Syria's (transitional) president in January 2025 and remains in power as of August 2026.
notes: Former HTS leader; appointed president January 2025; still president in July 2026 statements.

claim: As of mid-2026 Syria seeks a security agreement (not full normalization) with Israel.
notes: Talks aim to reactivate 1974 disengagement lines and secure Israeli withdrawal from post-Assad positions; Syria will not concede the Golan; Israel demands demilitarized SW Syria and Druze protection. No agreement signed as of 14 Aug 2026.

claim: A Gaza hostage/ceasefire deal took effect on 19 January 2025.
notes: Phased deal announced 15 January 2025; effective 11:15 local on 19 January.

claim: Phase 1 of the January 2025 deal covered 33 hostages over 42 days in exchange for ~1,900 Palestinian prisoners.
notes: 33 hostages listed (returned as 25 living + 8 deceased); Israel said it would release ~1,900 prisoners in this stage; Phase 2 never concluded.

claim: Israel resumed large-scale strikes in Gaza on 18 March 2025, ending the ceasefire.
notes: 400+ killed on the first night; Israel cited Hamas refusal of Witkoff bridge proposals to release more hostages.

claim: Israel and Iran fought a 12-day war from 13 to 24 June 2025.
notes: Israel's Operation Rising Lion opened 13 June 2025; ceasefire effective 24 June 2025.

claim: The US struck Fordow, Natanz and Isfahan on 21-22 June 2025 (Operation Midnight Hammer).
notes: 125 aircraft; 14 GBU-57 MOPs on Fordow and Natanz; Tomahawks on Isfahan; strikes landed ~1:30-2:10am local 22 June (evening 21 June US time). Damage 'extremely severe' per JCS but degree of program setback disputed.

claim: CSIS assessed in August 2025 that Iran's nuclear program was badly damaged but ~400 kg of 60% HEU is unaccounted for.
notes: Rodgers/Williams/Bermudez, CSIS PONI, 6 Aug 2025; Pickaxe Mountain facility untargeted; framed the moment as a diplomatic window.

claim: Trump announced a 20-point Gaza peace plan on 29 September 2025.
notes: Announced at the White House with Netanyahu (reported 29/30 September 2025); basis of the October framework and the Board of Peace.

claim: Israel and Hamas agreed the first phase of the Trump plan around 8-9 October 2025, with a ceasefire effective 10 October 2025.
notes: Trump announced the deal 8 October; signed 9 October; ceasefire and IDF pullback followed within 24 hours.

claim: Under the October 2025 ceasefire the IDF withdrew to a 'yellow line', retaining roughly 53% of Gaza.
notes: Yellow Line divides Gaza: ~47% Palestinian-controlled west of the line, ~53% Israeli-controlled east of it, pending later phases.

claim: All 20 living hostages were released on 13 October 2025.
notes: Released in two groups (7, then 13 named in the PMO announcement); exchanged for ~1,950-2,000 Palestinian prisoners/detainees; 4 deceased hostages returned the same day; Sharm el-Sheikh summit and Trump Knesset speech.

claim: The UN Security Council endorsed the Gaza framework via Resolution 2803 on 17 November 2025.
notes: Adopted 13-0-2 (China, Russia abstained); welcomes Board of Peace as transitional administration; authorizes International Stabilization Force through (initially) 2027.

claim: The remains of the final hostage, Staff Sgt. Ran Gvili, were returned in January 2026.
notes: Returned 26 January 2026 after ~842-843 days; Herzog: first time since 2014 with no Israeli hostages in Gaza. Exact date verified: 2026-01-26.

claim: A new US-Israel war with Iran began in February 2026.
notes: REAL, not fictional. Launched 28 February 2026 after Iran refused to end all enrichment; ~900 strikes in first 12 hours; goals included destroying nuclear/missile capability and regime change. Package claim 'Feb-April 2026 war' is accurate: conditional ceasefire declared 8 April 2026.

claim: Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei was killed on 28 February 2026.
notes: Killed in Israeli strike on his Tehran compound during the opening of the 2026 war (per officials briefed, reported by Washington Post).

claim: Mojtaba Khamenei succeeded his father as Iran's Supreme Leader in March 2026.
notes: Assumed office 8 March 2026 amid an unprecedented succession crisis; first father-to-son transfer; considered more hardline, IRGC-aligned.

claim: Iran closed the Strait of Hormuz in 2026.
notes: REAL. Declared closed 4 March 2026 (CRS gives 4 March; some accounts say late March for full blockage); reopened toll-free ~17 June under the MoU; closed again after early-July breakdown; effectively closed as of mid-August 2026 (~1 transit on 9 Aug vs ~73/day normal).

claim: A conditional US/Israel-Iran ceasefire was declared on 8 April 2026.
notes: Repeatedly strained; renewed US strikes on Iran on 7 May 2026; formalization attempted via the June MoU.

claim: A 2026 Israel-Hezbollah war took place (claimed March-June 2026).
notes: REAL, with a date correction: began 2 March 2026 (Hezbollah fire after Khamenei's killing); major combat through spring incl. Litani crossing, Bint Jbeil, Khiam; NOT cleanly ended by June — framework of 26 June rejected by Hezbollah, partial Israeli withdrawals late July, talks and sporadic fighting continuing into August 2026.

claim: On 8 April 2026 Israel launched its heaviest attacks of the war on Lebanon.
notes: At least 357 killed; came immediately after the Iran-front ceasefire announcement.

claim: The 2026 Lebanon war caused mass casualties and displacement.
notes: Wikipedia-cited tallies: 4,300+ Lebanese civilians killed, 12,000+ injured, 1.2M+ displaced; ~40 Israeli soldiers and 3 civilians killed; 1,000-2,500 Hezbollah fighters killed (estimates vary). Figures likely to be revised; treat totals as approximate.

claim: A temporary Israel-Hezbollah ceasefire began 16 April 2026 and was extended multiple times.
notes: Initial 10-day truce; interrupted by flare-ups (e.g., late-April strikes reported by Al Jazeera 27 April 2026).

claim: The US and Iran signed a memorandum of understanding in June 2026 (Islamabad Memorandum).
notes: REAL. Announced 14 June, signed 17 June 2026 by Trump, Pezeshkian, and Pakistani PM Shehbaz Sharif (Versailles/Tehran/Islamabad); Pakistan-Qatar mediation; 14 points: ceasefire, Hormuz reopening, blockade end, 60-day final-deal window, reconstruction concept. Israel objected and was not a party.

claim: The June 2026 US-Iran memorandum collapsed in July 2026.
notes: Iran struck commercial vessels off its 'preapproved route' 6-7 July; Trump declared the MoU 'over' on 8 July; renewed US strikes and naval blockade of Iranian ports followed; Iran-Oman channel on a Hormuz route active in early August.

claim: Benjamin Netanyahu is Israel's prime minister as of August 2026, with elections scheduled.
notes: Knesset adjourned/dissolved 17 July 2026; general election set for 27 October 2026 — first on-schedule election in ~4 decades; widely framed as a referendum on Netanyahu's handling of Oct 7 and the war; Likud leads polls but coalition math difficult; Gadi Eisenkot the main challenger.

claim: Gaza status August 2026: disarmament dispute between the Board of Peace and Israel; ISF embryonic; IDF beyond the yellow line.
notes: Early Aug 2026: Trump announced a Board of Peace 'historic agreement' on complete Hamas disarmament; Netanyahu said Israel did not agree to its terms and won't withdraw until Hamas fully disarms; IDF reportedly expanded from the yellow line toward an 'orange line' (~65% of Gaza vs ~53% at ceasefire); ISF has a US commander, only ~5 troop-contributing countries pledged, small deployment; Board of Peace chaired by Trump; NCAG/transitional committee handles civil administration; Israeli strikes continue episodically.

claim: Iran's nuclear program status is opaque as of August 2026.
notes: No IAEA inspectors since June 2025; ~400 kg of 60% HEU unaccounted for; Feb 2026 war aimed at nuclear/missile destruction but no confirmed evidence the program was eliminated; nuclear commitments were part of the collapsed June 2026 MoU.

claim: Lebanon/Hezbollah status August 2026: disarmament-conditioned framework, partial Israeli withdrawal, unresolved.
notes: June 26 framework ties Israeli withdrawal (Israel holds roughly a fifth of Lebanon) to full Hezbollah disarmament; Hezbollah rejects; Lebanese Army running 'pilot area' takeovers; Israel-Lebanon talks resumed in Rome 4 Aug 2026; Israeli operations against Hezbollah infrastructure continue in the border zone.

claim: Source S09 (AP article apnews.com/article/1c1e810598dd3323bcb5f0f771362471) exists and supports package claims.
notes: apnews.com is unfetchable by tool and searches for this article ID returned no hits; cannot confirm the article's existence or content. Any claim resting solely on S09 should be re-sourced.

claim: UN Digital Library record 4093207 is UNSC Resolution 2803 (2025).
notes: digitallibrary.un.org blocks automated access (403) and the specific record number could not be confirmed via search; the resolution itself (S/RES/2803, 17 Nov 2025, 13-0-2) is fully verified via UN press release and full text mirrors. Use press.un.org as the citation instead.

claim: Hostage arithmetic across the war is consistent: 251 taken; 105 released Nov 2023; 30 living + bodies returned under the Jan 2025 deal; 20 living + 28 deceased remained at the Oct 2025 deal; last body returned 26 Jan 2026.
notes: 48 hostages (20 living, 28 deceased) remained when the October 2025 deal took effect; all 20 living freed 13 Oct 2025; deceased returned in batches through 26 Jan 2026 (Ran Gvili last).

claim: The UK recognized the State of Palestine in September 2025.
notes: Per Commons Library CBP-10235: UK recognized Palestine in September 2025 with provisional 1967-line borders.
